newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujitsu's group cash flow to rise sharply in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu's group cash flow to rise sharply in 97/98.

text.p: Fujitsu Ltd said on Wednesday that its group-based cash flow is likely to reach 410 billion yen in the year to March 1998, up 33 percent from the previous year.
A spokesman for the firm said the company anticipates the sharp rise as it expects its semiconductor chip and personal computer operations to turn profitable in the current business year.

Cash flow is cash earnings including net income and depreciation of assets, such as plant and equipment. The cost of asset depreciation earmarked for a certain business year reduces a firm's income tax.
Fujitsu also expects earnings at its overseas computer units to improve this year, the spokesman said.
He said the increase in asset depreciation as result of a large amount of capital investment in the last few years had helped to boost cash earnings.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Wednesday that Fujitsu's group-based cash flow would likely exceed Toshiba Corp's expected consolidated cash flow of 375 billion yen in 1997/98, the first time this had happened.
